title: Farol Protocol v0.4 — action/invoke
description: Request and response envelopes for the action/invoke method. See protocol/SPEC.md §5.3 for the normative round-trip and §7.2 for its dedicated timeout budget (RPC_TIMEOUT_ACTION, distinct from RPC_TIMEOUT_CONTROL used by handshake/hello and widget/get). References ActionTarget from handshake.schema.json and GitRepository/VpnStatusItem/ContainerStatusItem from widget.schema.json. Evolved from v0.3 (protocol/schema/v0.3/action.schema.json, retained as-is): ActionInvokeResult, previously a oneOf of repo/vpn_status, gains a third branch, container (research.md D4, D11, data-model.md §1.6), returned by the new docker-containers reference plugin's docker.container.start/stop/restart actions. The wire already emitted by git-local ({"repo": {...}}) and openfortivpn-gui ({"vpn_status": {...}}) keeps validating against the first two branches unchanged - this is an additive change; the three branches remain disjoint by top-level key (repo/vpn_status/container), so the untagged disambiguation here stays structural and sound, unlike WidgetItems in widget.schema.json (research.md D12).

action_id.description: Must match the `id` of an ActionDeclaration the plugin previously declared (in the handshake result and/or a widget/get response) for the given target, with enabled=true.

target.description: MUST be echoed back verbatim from the target of the ActionDeclaration that motivated this invocation - the core MUST NOT reconstruct a target on its own.

ActionInvokeResult.title: ActionInvokeResult
ActionInvokeResult.description: Result of a successful action invocation. Discriminated by which single property is present - repo (git-local's fetch action, unchanged since v0.2), vpn_status (openfortivpn-gui's connect/disconnect actions, since v0.3), or container (new in v0.4, research.md D4, D11, data-model.md §1.6). For the git-local reference plugin's git.fetch action, repo is the post-fetch repository state. For the openfortivpn-gui reference plugin's vpn.connect/vpn.disconnect actions, vpn_status is the post-action VpnStatusItem. For the docker-containers reference plugin's docker.container.start/stop/restart actions, container is the post-action ContainerStatusItem in full, not just the new state, because enabled of the three ActionDeclaration changes with state and the core MUST NOT recompute it on its own (protocol/SPEC.md §5.3, research.md D4/D11) - same reasoning as vpn_status. The wire already emitted by git-local ({"repo": {...}}) and openfortivpn-gui ({"vpn_status": {...}}) keeps validating against the first two branches, unchanged.

repo.description: Updated state of the target repository after the action ran.

oneOf.title: ActionInvokeResultVpnStatus
oneOf.description: Since v0.3 (research.md D2/D4-D5, data-model.md §1.5) - returned by vpn.connect/vpn.disconnect.

vpn_status.description: Updated VPN connection status after the action ran.

oneOf.title: ActionInvokeResultContainer
oneOf.description: New in v0.4 (research.md D4, D11, data-model.md §1.6) - returned by docker.container.start/stop/restart.

container.description: Updated container state after the action ran, in full - not only the new state, since enabled of its three ActionDeclaration depends on state.

ActionInvokeResponseError.title: ActionInvokeResponseError
ActionInvokeResponseError.description: E.g. code -32001 / reason "fetch_failed" when the underlying action execution failed, or code -32002 / reason "action_timeout" synthesized by the core when RPC_TIMEOUT_ACTION elapses. MUST NOT cause the plugin process to exit (protocol/SPEC.md §8.3) - the plugin keeps responding to subsequent requests. Never marks the plugin connection unavailable by itself.
